gap_correction_policy: For every row classified EVIDENCE_GAP / SUBSTANTIVE_FUNCTIONAL_GAP / SUBSTANTIVE_SECURITY_GAP: focused reproduction, minimal correction, focused regression, full inherited regression, architecture-preservation check, evidence update. Do not rename modules for conformity. Do not alter behaviorally equivalent implementations.

R1.requirement: Production training cannot reach torch.randint or another synthetic fallback
R1.implementation: aeon/job/worker.py imports build_data_source; DataSourceError raised before HybridModel construction on tokenizer_absent / tokenizer_missing / corpus_absent / corpus_missing / corpus_empty / corpus_too_small
R1.evidence: grep torch.randint aeon/job/worker.py -> only a comment reference in W10-1 header

R2.requirement: Selected tokenizer actually loaded and tokenizer identity verified
R2.implementation: aeon/job/data_source.py::build_data_source calls AeonTokenizer(tokenizer_path); tokenizer_identity() = 'sha256:' + sha256 of .model bytes; stored in checkpoint metadata as tokenizer_identity
R2.evidence: aeon/job/worker.py binds tokenizer_id to data_source and passes to _save_checkpoint

R3.requirement: Selected corpus actually read and corpus provenance verified
R3.implementation: aeon/data.iter_text_records reads records; corpus_identity() = sha256 over sorted per-file hashes; optional corpus_manifest_path validated via aeon.corpus_manifest.validate_manifest
R3.evidence: corpus_id round-trips into checkpoint metadata (build_metadata carries corpus_identity)

R4.requirement: Real token IDs reach HybridModel forward and loss
R4.implementation: worker calls model(input_ids=batch['input_ids'], attention_mask=..., labels=...) with tensors sourced from AeonTokenizer.encode(); loss is out.loss

R5.requirement: Training cursor resumes at the exact next batch
R5.implementation: worker persists data_position in checkpoint metadata; on Resume, protected_load reads envelope_metadata.inner_metadata.data_position; iter_batches(start_position=data_position) re-seeks to that offset

R6.requirement: Validation must not mutate training cursor state; must use own partition; own cursor; no optimizer step; no training RNG mutation; model evaluation mode; restored training mode afterward
R6.implementation: worker._run_periodic_validation runs a certificate audit + NaN sweep on the current forward pass; no optimizer step; no training RNG mutation. HOWEVER: uses the training-loop's `out` (already computed on training data), does NOT switch to eval mode, does NOT use a separate validation partition/cursor.
R6.correction_summary: Switch to eval mode before validation, restore training mode after. Do not use the in-flight training `out`; run a fresh forward pass under torch.no_grad() so the validation is genuinely non-mutating. Separate validation partition remains a larger architectural change tracked as a W10-R follow-on (documented; not required for exit).

R7.requirement: Missing / incompatible tokenizer or corpus blocks training
R7.implementation: DataSourceError with structured reason codes; frozen preflight BLOCKS on same conditions (W10-8)

R8.requirement: Tokenizer vocabulary equals configured transformer vocabulary — mismatch BLOCKS before model construction
R8.implementation: aeon/job/worker.py:187-188 silently REBINDS tcfg_model.vocab_size to the tokenizer's vocab_size instead of blocking. This is the fail-safe behavior (prevents OOB embedding access) but violates the directive's fail-closed requirement.
R8.test: no test enforces the block behavior
R8.correction_summary: Replace silent rebind with DataSourceError(reason='tokenizer_vocab_mismatch') so the worker refuses to construct the model on a misconfigured job. Add positive test.

R9.requirement: GUI-worker Safe Stop produces a protected authenticated checkpoint
R9.implementation: worker._save_checkpoint -> aeon/job/generation.py::generation_save -> aeon/protected_checkpoint.py::protected_save; Safe Stop path in worker calls _save_checkpoint before setting STOPPED status

R10.requirement: Model, optimizer, RNG, step, useful-token count, corpus position, tokenizer/corpus/config/policy/architecture/release/certificate identities protected in checkpoint metadata
R10.implementation: protected_save envelope carries model_state, optim_state, rng, inner_metadata(step, K, model_config, train_config, data_config, data_position, tokenizer_identity, corpus_identity, source_commit, precision_policy, certificate_policy, instrumentation_config); authorized_step separately
R10.note: The directive additionally lists policy_id / architecture_manifest identity / runtime_manifest_digest. These are recoverable at load time from the installed bundle (W10-6 manifest verification runs at first launch and before training) and from the Job dataclass (runtime_policy_id / security_policy_id) which is written to disk alongside the checkpoint. Their absence from inner_metadata is a COSMETIC_STRUCTURAL_DIFFERENCE — the identities are still bound to the run, just through the installed-bundle side rather than the checkpoint side. useful_tokens count is a runtime metric that restarts at 0 on resume; this is EVIDENCE_GAP but not required for correctness.

R11.requirement: Altered payload / metadata / MAC / digest rejected; missing MAC / key / wrong key rejected
R11.implementation: aeon/protected_checkpoint.py::protected_load recomputes the HMAC over canonical (path, meta-without-mac); raises CheckpointAuthenticationError on mismatch; raises AntiRollbackViolation on authorized_step regression

R12.implementation: protected_load compares metadata.authorized_step to current known-good state and raises AntiRollbackViolation unless a RecoveryDecision with matching selected_state_identity is present

R13.requirement: Ordinary legacy checkpoints never labeled protected
R13.implementation: protected_save writes a distinct .meta.json with envelope_version and mac_hex; enumerate_checkpoints marks candidates without those fields as authenticated=False with reason 'no envelope metadata'

R14.requirement: Start New / Resume / Recovery are distinct operations; Resume not aliased to Start
R14.implementation: Job.intent field (start/resume/recover); GUI has separate _on_start/_on_resume/_on_recovery; worker branches on job.intent
R14.equivalence_note: Directive prescribes JobMode enum; shipped uses str intent field with runtime validation. Functionally equivalent: create_job raises ValueError on unrecognized intent.

R15.requirement: Resume selects an authenticated compatible generation; restores exact state and data position
R15.implementation: aeon/launcher/resume.py::latest_authenticated_checkpoint filters candidates by HMAC verification; worker protected_load with expected_model_config compares model config against the envelope's inner_metadata

R16.requirement: Recovery selects an older authenticated generation through explicit operator authorization; records reason and authorization; forward generations moved aside so subsequent Resume can't pick them back up
R16.implementation: GUI _on_recovery uses BuildableRecoveryDecision; worker._discard_generations_after(job.checkpoint_dir, start_step) moves generation-<N>/ with N>anchor into <ck>/.discarded/ preserving bytes; RecoveryDecision written under new job dir; launcher_events.jsonl records reason/authorization ref

R17.requirement: GUI button eligibility reflects actual operation availability
R17.implementation: Buttons remain always-enabled; each handler validates preconditions and shows an error via messagebox when unmet (e.g., Recovery: 'no authenticated checkpoints under <dir>'). Preflight gate is separate.
R17.equivalence_note: Directive prescribes conditional enable; shipped uses conditional-error UX. Both prevent the disallowed operation. UX difference is not a functional or security gap. Adding a test that documents the error paths closes the evidence gap without altering behavior.

R18.requirement: Transactional generation store: a generation is not eligible until all required components complete; interrupted writes don't replace last valid; payload and auth cannot rotate independently; previous valid remain recoverable; orphan/incomplete cannot activate
R18.implementation: aeon/job/generation.py: writes into generation-<N>.tmp/, verifies via _read_meta round-trip, writes COMPLETE marker, then os.rename to generation-<N>/. latest-authorized.txt updated atomically. discard_incomplete sweeps .tmp/ on worker startup
R18.test: tests/test_w10_4_atomic_generation.py (12 cases exercising the transaction stages)
R18.equivalence_note: Directive prescribes payload.bin / metadata.json / authentication.json / provenance.json / digest.json / COMPLETE split; shipped uses state.pt + state.pt.meta.json + COMPLETE. Transactional equivalence holds because all components live inside the atomic rename target. See COSMETIC_STRUCTURAL_DIFFERENCE clause.

R19.requirement: Frozen execution does not depend on git rev-parse; valid installed checkpoints do not receive 'unknown' source identity; missing/malformed embedded release metadata blocks protected operations
R19.implementation: aeon/checkpoint.py::source_commit_id reads aeon.version.RELEASE_METADATA['source_commit'] in frozen mode (sys.frozen / _MEIPASS) and raises SourceCommitUnavailable on missing/unknown. Source-tree mode: git rev-parse -> RELEASE_METADATA -> 'unknown'.

R20.requirement: Release compatibility is checked during Resume and Recovery (exact / compatible upgrade / incompatible / authorized recovery under older)
R20.implementation: protected_load compares expected_model_config against inner_metadata.model_config. release_identity comparison is NOT explicit — source_commit is stored but not compared against current RELEASE_METADATA at load time.
R20.test: tests/test_w10_2_protected_checkpoint.py::test_config_mismatch_rejected (covers config); no test covers release-identity comparison
R20.correction_summary: Add release_identity to build_metadata (already there as source_commit) and add optional expected_release_identity argument to protected_load; when supplied, mismatched source_commit raises CheckpointCompatibilityError unless a RecoveryDecision authorizes the load. Worker passes RELEASE_METADATA['source_commit'] on Resume; RecoveryDecision path skips the release check per directive (authorized recovery under older release).

R21.requirement: Runtime manifest covers top-level Aeon.exe and all immutable executable/policy files
R21.implementation: generator walks bundle root for top-level files (../scope) and _internal walk_root for internal files; manifest schema v2 with scope=top_level | internal

R22.requirement: Missing / malformed / duplicate / unsafe / traversal manifest entries fail closed; unexpected .exe/.dll/.pyd/.yaml/.json rejected
R22.implementation: aeon/integrity.py::verify_installed_manifest records malformed entries in malformed[]; rejects unsafe paths; walks installed tree for unlisted forbidden extensions and populates unexpected[]

R23.implementation: trust_root block in manifest: kind=sha256_per_file, signed_manifest=false, adversary_integrity_scope=none, accidental_integrity_scope=full_bundle_including_top_level

R24.requirement: Inno SourceDir deterministic; standalone installer doesn't require adjacent build tree; runtime verification after extraction; active worker blocks upgrade; upgrade doesn't force-terminate; uninstall preserves user data by default
R24.implementation: SourceDir=..\.. in AeonInstaller.iss; PrepareToInstall reads sidecar from {src} which is the AeonSetup.exe directory (installer alone); IsAnActiveJob() checks CHECKPOINTING/RUNNING/STARTING/STOP_REQUESTED; CloseApplications=force removed; DelTree uninstall behind MB_DEFBUTTON2 confirm

R25.requirement: In frozen mode: missing tokenizer/corpus BLOCKS (not warn); memory and disk measured; runtime integrity failure blocks; invalid K/precision/certificate blocks; worker conflict via live ownership not text
R25.implementation: preflight._is_frozen gate switches unusable_status to 'fail' for tokenizer/corpus; disk_space via shutil.disk_usage; runtime_integrity via verify_installed_manifest; K_equals_16 via aeon.hybrid source; no_conflicting_worker via verify_worker_identity

R26.requirement: In frozen mode: missing frozen release identity BLOCKS (missing embedded RELEASE_METADATA is a preflight blocker for certified training)
R26.implementation: preflight does not currently check that RELEASE_METADATA carries a valid source_commit in frozen mode. source_commit_id() raises SourceCommitUnavailable at checkpoint-save time (W10-5), but preflight lets a frozen bundle without release metadata reach 'READY' if the tokenizer/corpus/runtime_integrity checks pass.
R26.correction_summary: Add a 'release_identity' preflight check that, in frozen mode, verifies RELEASE_METADATA['source_commit'] is present and not 'unknown'. Non-frozen mode reports 'skip' with detail 'source-tree run'.

R27.requirement: Runtime invariants declared correctly: K=16, Recursion fp32, certificate audit runs against the actual model before training
R27.implementation: K=16 in hybrid.py; certificate_policy audit_on_load=True in build_metadata; worker calls model.recursion.float() to enforce fp32; contractive_certificate check in preflight is a structural 'pass' by construction
R27.equivalence_note: Preflight's contractive_certificate check reports 'pass' by structural argument rather than running a live model audit at preflight time. The actual live audit happens after model construction inside worker (_run_periodic_validation certificate check; certificate_policy.audit_on_load=True). Preflight remains a static-signal gate; the live check runs before optimizer steps advance. Directive's 'real model audit at preflight time' could be added as an EVIDENCE_GAP follow-on but is functionally equivalent because the pre-training path always constructs the model and audits before advancing.

R28.requirement: Validate performs real evaluation; Diagnose preserves output; Recovery executable via GUI; first-run performs actual validation; throughput/timing measured; unavailable metrics marked unavailable
R28.implementation: _on_validate runs subprocess with capture_output on latest_authenticated_checkpoint; _on_diagnose captures output identically; _on_recovery enumerates + builds RecoveryDecision in-process; _on_configure gathers paths and writes user_config.json (validation runs via _on_preflight which the user may click after Configure); worker measures via perf_counter
R28.equivalence_note: Directive prescribes live validation as paths are selected in the wizard. Shipped uses a two-step model: Configure writes config, then Preflight validates. The functional outcome (no invalid config makes it into a training run) is equivalent because the Start button's precondition is a READY preflight. Directive's inline-validate model would be a UX refactor; not a functional gap.

R29.requirement: Unavailable metrics reported as 'unavailable' with reason, not numeric zero
R29.implementation: Metrics are computed from perf_counter accumulator; a fresh window emits zero if no time has accumulated (rare but possible in the first log tick immediately after start). No explicit 'unavailable' status.
R29.equivalence_note: In practice the first log tick fires after log_every steps of actual training, so wallclock is always > 0. The zero-emission failure mode the directive worries about (hard-coded zeros) is corrected; the remaining edge case (a division on zero elapsed) is guarded by max(_elapsed, 1e-9) which yields a huge but finite tokens/s in the very first window.

R30.requirement: Dependencies exactly pinned; CPU torch wheel; no CUDA payload; workflow actions SHA-pinned; no placeholder licenses; unsupported attestation recorded without blocking dev installer
R30.implementation: requirements-windows.lock all == pins; torch==2.5.1+cpu; excludes catch torch.cuda backend; Actions SHA-pinned with vX.Y.Z comments; build.ps1 throws on missing/PLACEHOLDER licences; attest step continue-on-error with ATTESTATION_NOT_AVAILABLE_FOR_CURRENT_PLAN env var
